summary: A one-paragraph announcement that the time limit for anonymous sampling use of the Multics system over the ARPANET was raised from one CPU minute to five, so that a real experiment could fit in one session. It is a service notice, not a protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 450 announces a longer time limit for anonymous sampling use of Multics over the network. The limit changed from one CPU minute to five.

subtitle: A change to the anonymous Multics session time limit.

tldr.problem: The time limit for anonymous sampling use of Multics over the network was one CPU minute.
tldr.mechanism: The limit was increased to five CPU minutes; the RFC also notes internal speedups.
tldr.outcome: The author says the change should allow substantive experiments in one session.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 450's status as Unknown. The RFC is a short service notice about Multics sampling use.

sections.title: The Previous Time Limit
sections.content: The RFC says anonymous sampling use of Multics over the network had a timeout of one CPU minute. It describes this as a limit on trial use of the system.
sections.plainLanguage: People trying Multics over the network had a one-CPU-minute time limit. The RFC announces a change to that limit.

sections.title: Five CPU Minutes for Sampling
sections.content:
In response to user demand and an extra bit of budget, the timeout was raised to five CPU minutes. The RFC also mentions internal speedups.

The author says these changes should let users carry out substantive experiments in a single session.
sections.plainLanguage: The new limit is five CPU minutes instead of one. The author says this and internal speedups should make meaningful experiments possible in one session.

sections.title: What the Notice Covers
sections.content: RFC 450 is a one-paragraph announcement about the sampling timeout and system speedups. It does not describe a protocol or provide details about the speedups.
sections.plainLanguage: This note reports a service change. It does not explain the internal speedups.
